why: Checking each part of the criterion: - **Says it's good and names what it's great at, tied to evidence:** It opens with "es un buen producto con una señal real" and names the strengths: NPS 62 as real love (conditionally), "nadie tenga que cobrar" as the core strength, and the 70% link-driven arrival as "lo mejor que tienes". This is specific and evidence-tied. - **Leads with ONE priority, everything else brief and subordinate:** There is a section titled "La única cosa que lo cambiaría todo" (turn the guest into the next organizer). But it is placed late, after a "Lo que está mal" section containing four numbered problems with sub-bullets, so the priority does not actually lead. - **Weakness sizing / second list of similar weight:** After praising, the reply gives a four-item problems list (pitch, 41% retention, last 10% of the ticket, no moat), each with bullets and proposals. Then it adds the "one thing", a "what to say no to" section, and a standard. The problems list carries weight similar to the priority, and the reply as a whole is not organized around one change. This matches the FAIL condition of "a second list of problems of similar weight". It also asserts things like "'10 segundos' es una promesa que no puedes cumplir" and "41 % ... puede ser humo" with some overreach, though it hedges with "puede". Questioning the retention measurement is legitimate, but the volume of criticism is spread out. The reply is not wholesale harsh and does name strengths, but it fails the structure requirement of a single leading priority with brief subordinate items.

The reply does name what is good and ties it to the evidence: NPS 62 and 70 % link acquisition show people send it on unprompted, and the guest experience of paying without installing anything is what the product really does well. It also questions whose retention the 41 % measures, which the criterion allows. It fails on structure and proportion: - **No single priority.** The "one change" (the straggler moment) comes only after a full section declaring "El pitch está roto" with three bullets and a rewrite, and after a section of number worries. It does not lead, and the other material is not brief or subordinate. - **Competing problem lists.** The pitch critique, the retention and link worries, and the "Dudas que me quedan" list (OCR errors, shared dishes and tips, where the money goes) all carry similar weight. It even says it does not rank the last list. That is the second list of problems the criterion warns against. - **Some inflation.** "Roto" for a pitch whose underlying product the evidence supports, and calling 41 % "demasiado bueno" for episodic use, lean toward harshness beyond the evidence.

The reply never says the product is good and never names what it does well. It opens by dismissing all three numbers ("los más fáciles de inflar... ninguno responde la pregunta"), and it calls the pitch "mentira". The evidence gives no grounds for that. It then stacks several lists of problems of similar weight: the numbers, the pitch, "lo que no dijiste", and four action items. It does not lead with one priority change or question. The harshness is inflated rather than sized to the evidence.

The reply passes on praise. It says the product is good, and it names the guest experience (open a link, tap your items, pay) as the excellent part. It ties that to the 70% link-arrival figure, which it calls the best data point. Questioning whose retention the 41% measures is also legitimate under the criterion, and the reply does not call the product a lie or a failure. It fails on structure and proportion. It does not lead with one priority and keep the rest brief. After the verdict and three questions, it opens a "Lo que está mal" section with three bullets of roughly equal weight: the pitch, the retention figure, and the mixed numbers hiding the organizer. Only then does it give "el único cambio". It then adds a three-item list of what to measure and a "what not to do" section. That is several problem and advice lists of similar weight after the priority, and they are not subordinate to it. The pitch critique is also fairly harsh ("vende una ausencia", "no me dice nada"), which leans toward manufactured severity.

The reply fails on several counts. - **No real praise.** It never says the product is good and names what it does well, tied to the evidence. The only nod is a closing line that the numbers are "un buen indicio de que el producto le gusta a quien lo usó". That is vague and buried at the end. It also opens by saying the numbers "menos prueban". - **No single priority.** It gives five sections of problems of similar weight (pitch, referral, retention, NPS, and a long list of missing business items), then a five-item action list. It does not lead with one change or question and keep the rest subordinate. - **Inflated weaknesses.** It dismisses the evidence wholesale: the 70% referral share is "no es crecimiento", the retention "huele mal", and the NPS "sufre de sesgo de supervivencia". It also speculates without grounds ("me juego a que la mediana está en minutos", competition, regulation, moat). It treats the pitch as probably false when the prompt only leaves that open.

The reply fails on several counts. - **No real praise.** It never says the product is good or names what it does well. The 41% retention, NPS 62 and 70% link-driven acquisition are each undercut as inflated, biased or merely "no other channel", not credited as evidence of one thing done well. - **Manufactured harshness.** It flatly states "El pitch es falso" without grounds, and the verdict opens by saying the metrics answer nothing. This dismisses the evidence wholesale. - **No single priority.** It gives a long list of six further problems (monetization, moat, ticket mess, trust, frequency) plus a separate list of five actions. These are of similar weight, and the problems are inflated rather than sized as what they are.
